name: Nadab (Aaron's son)
title: Aaron's firstborn son
summary: Nadab was the firstborn son of Aaron, Israel's first high priest. He was consecrated for priestly service along with his father and brothers, but died together with his brother Abihu when they offered unauthorized fire before the Lord. His death served as a warning about the importance of approaching God in the prescribed manner.

keyEvents.title: They saw the God of Israel on Mount Sinai
keyEvents.description: Nadab was among the seventy elders who were allowed to go up Mount Sinai with Moses, Aaron, and Abihu, where they saw the God of Israel and ate and drank in his presence.

keyEvents.title: Consecration for priestly service
keyEvents.description: Nadab was consecrated for priestly service along with his father Aaron and his brothers at the tabernacle, as God had commanded Moses.

keyEvents.title: Offers unauthorized fire
keyEvents.description: Nadab and his brother Abihu each took their censer, put fire in it, added incense, and offered unauthorized fire before the Lord, which he had not commanded them.

keyEvents.title: Condemned by God
keyEvents.description: Fire came out from the Lord and consumed Nadab and Abihu, so that they died before the Lord. Moses explained that God must be treated as holy by those who approach him.

keyEvents.title: Burial outside the camp
keyEvents.description: Nadab's cousins carried him and Abihu out of the camp in their priestly garments, just as Moses had commanded. Aaron and his remaining sons were forbidden to mourn publicly.
